stories.headline: Elly De La Cruz hits 2-run HR, Reds beat Dodgers 6-2 to delay NL West title
stories.summary: — Elly De La Cruz hit a two-run homer and the Cincinnati Reds at least temporarily prevented the Los Angeles Dodgers from clinching the NL West title with a 6-2 victory on Wednesday night.
stories.body:
CINCINNATI -- — Elly De La Cruz hit a two-run homer and the Cincinnati Reds at least temporarily prevented the Los Angeles Dodgers from clinching the NL West title with a 6-2 victory on Wednesday night.


The Dodgers (92-60) needed a win or a loss by San Diego to win their fifth straight NL West crown and 13th in 14 seasons. The Padres played at Colorado later Wednesday.


Left-hander Blake Snell started for the Dodgers but departed after one inning with left groin tightness. Snell, who threw a no-hitter for the Giants in his last appearance in Great American Ball Park, faced three batters, allowing a hit with a strikeout on 19 pitches.


Blake Treinen took over in the second as the first of six relievers used by Los Angeles.


Mookie Betts singled off Andrew Abbott in the third and scored on Will Smith's double to put the Dodgers ahead 1-0. Abbott allowed a run on three hits with five walks in 4 2/3 innings. Tejay Antone (3-2), the third of six Cincinnati pitchers, got the last out of the sixth.


De La Cruz's homer off Seth Halvorsen (1-2), his 28th of the season, put the Reds ahead 2-1 in the third. It was De La Cruz's fifth longball against the Dodgers this season, most of any opposing player.


Dane Myers' homer off Bobby Miller, his seventh, extended the Reds' lead to 3-1 in the fifth.


Juan Brito's RBI single made it 4-2 in the sixth.


TJ Friedl singled with the bases loaded in the seventh to drive in two runs. Sal Stewart was thrown out at the plate by Dodgers center fielder Tommy Edman to end the inning.


The Dodgers stranded 12 runners and went 0 for 11 with runners in scoring position.


Up next
RHP Brady Singer (6-14, 5.38 ERA) will start Thursday's series finale for the Reds. The Dodgers had not announced their starter.

stories.headline: Messi nets 100th Miami goal en route to Campeones Cup win
stories.summary: Lionel Messi scored his 100th goal for Inter Miami in all competitions after heading home the opener in a 2-0 win over Cruz Azul in the Campeones Cup on Wednesday night at Nu Stadium.
stories.body:
MIAMI -- Lionel Messi scored his 100th goal for Inter Miami in all competitions after heading home the opener in a 2-0 win over Cruz Azul in the Campeones Cup on Wednesday night at Nu Stadium.

Messi's goal put Miami up 1-0 in the annual match between the champion of MLS and Liga MX before a late header from Casemiro put the game away to hand new coach Cristian "Kily" González a trophy in his first match in charge.

Luis Suarez set up the opener in the 24th minute with a perfectly lofted cross from the right side that Messi ran onto, outjumping his marker and scoring a rare goal with his head.

González led his first training session with Inter Miami on Tuesday after landing in Miami from Argentina earlier in the morning. The team had reached an agreement with González to replace interim coach Guillermo Hoyos on Aug. 27, but he was unable to take over until receiving his work permit.

His first game as Miami coach will be one to remember with Messi scoring his 100th goal for the club and the team picking up a trophy on the night.

Messi, a World Cup winner in 2022, reached the milestone in only 115 games for Inter Miami, marking the quickest he has recorded 100 goals for any team he has represented. Messi previously reached the mark with Barcelona in 188 games and 174 games with Argentina.

Since joining Miami in 2023, Messi has 76 goals in MLS, 14 in Leagues Cup action, eight in the Concacaf Champions Cup and one at the FIFA Club World Cup.

Messi made an instant impact in south Florida since signing with Miami, leading the Herons to the 2023 Leagues Cup title just weeks after marking his debut against Cruz Azul -- the team against which he scored his first Miami goal.

The Inter Miami captain also guided the team to the 2024 Supporters' Shield -- setting the record for most points (74) in an MLS season -- and starred in the playoffs during a run to the 2025 MLS Cup title last year.

Messi has now scored 929 goals for club and country during his career and leads MLS with 19 goals in 22 games so far this season.

stories.headline: Buccaneers' Zampese says Browns messed up by trading Mayfield
stories.summary: Buccaneers assistant coach Ken Zampease, who was Baker Mayfield's QB coach with the Browns in 2018, says Cleveland messed up by trading the QB.
stories.body:
TAMPA, Fla. -- Buccaneers senior offensive assistant/pass game specialist Ken Zampese was with quarterback Baker Mayfield just one year in Cleveland, but he saw enough then and now that has him convinced the Browns made a mistake trading him in 2022.

"They had the guy," Zampese, who was the Browns quarterbacks coach in 2018, told ESPN ahead of the teams' matchup Sunday in Tampa. "They had the guy and they gave him up."

Mayfield faced the Browns in Week 1 in 2022 with the Carolina Panthers, but Jacoby Brissett was Cleveland's starting quarterback as Deshaun Watson was serving an 11-game suspension. The Panthers lost 26-24. This time, it will be Watson on the other side of the ball.

"The year we were there, we were one of the best offenses in the NFL the second half of that season, 5-3, in a place that was -- before that season started -- 1-31," Zampese said of Mayfield. "The script got flipped and the city came alive because they finally drafted a quarterback that worked out for them and they mucked it up. They mucked it up."

When asked if he thought the Browns shared his sentiment, Zampese said, "Oh, I don't know. It doesn't matter. We got the guy we wanted [in Tampa] and that's what's important."

Mayfield went 29-30 as a starter with the Browns, leading them to the playoffs in 2020, where they clinched their first postseason victory in 26 years with a 48-37 win at the Pittsburgh Steelers. He threw for 263 yards and three touchdowns in that performance before losing to the Kansas City Chiefs 22-17 in the AFC divisional round.

That was the high point and what Mayfield has chosen to think about from his time in Cleveland.

"With any experience, there's ups and downs, good and bad," Mayfield said. "Ultimately, you remember the good more so than the bad -- the first time having a playoff win since '94 there and going on the road and doing it in Pittsburgh. So it's a lot of good memories there. A lot of teammates that are friends for life."

But Mayfield struggled with injuries the following year in 2021, including a torn labrum in his non-throwing shoulder sustained in Week 2. He wore a harness to stabilize the joint, but then-offensive coordinator Alex Van Pelt said it affected his throwing mechanics. He also navigated knee and foot injuries. On top of that, Mayfield faced death threats on social media, and public criticism from teammate Odell Beckham Jr.'s father.

Mayfield had also received criticism for some of the things he said publicly, such as calling former head coach Hue Jackson "fake." His brother Matthew had also taken to social media to express his own dissatisfaction with the Browns in 2018.

"Whenever a quarterback is drafted that high, everything's set up for you to fail. You haven't done this yet. You haven't accomplished this yet. I compared you with this guy in the history of the organization. I mean, goodness gracious," Zampese told ESPN.

In March 2022 -- two months after undergoing shoulder surgery -- Mayfield learned through social media that the team was pursuing Watson in a trade with the Houston Texans. He told ESPN's Adam Schefter at the time, "It's in the mutual interest of both sides for us to move on. The relationship is too far gone to mend. It's in the best interests of both sides to move on."

The Browns handed Watson a fully guaranteed five-year, $230 million contract. In July 2022, they traded Mayfield to the Panthers for a conditional draft pick.

The Panthers released him in December of that year, and he had a brief stint with the Los Angeles Rams, where he "fell in love with football again," playing in Sean McVay's system. That's also where he met his eventual Bucs offensive coordinator Liam Coen -- now the head coach of the Jacksonville Jaguars -- and his current offensive coordinator in Tampa, Zac Robinson.

The stint with the Rams led to a one-year "prove it" deal with the Bucs in 2023, culminating in an NFC South title that season and a wild-card playoff victory over the Philadelphia Eagles. He would lead the Bucs to another division title in 2024. An injury-marred season for Mayfield and the Bucs set them back in 2025, but he was rewarded with a three-year, $165 million contract extension.

"I think for me it goes back to the faith, looking up and knowing that no matter what happens, if I control what I can control, I'm doing things the right way," Mayfield said. "Obviously I want to win as an ultracompetitor, that's what you want to do at all times. So having trust in that, having faith in that and taking it one day at a time."

Mayfield told the "4th & South" podcast this summer that he has had this Week 2 game circled since the schedule was revealed.

But in Week 1, he fumbled the ball three times in a season-opening 33-27 loss at the Cincinnati Bengals. When the conversation in postgame quickly shifted to Cleveland, his response was more measured: "Obviously, there's history there -- there's no way to go around that," Mayfield said.

Much of his focus this week has been on the details of his performance rather than the opponent. Zampese says he believes that will help him manage his emotions, along with his ability to compartmentalize.

"Yeah, it's part of the job. And the guys that don't play the position very long, if you're ruled by your emotions that way, you're going to have a roller-coaster ride," Zampese said. "It's the ability to remove yourself from the ups and downs of that or just use it to provide energy and juice for the next situation to get into rather than thinking of the past and letting it bog you down."

Watson was suspended 11 games to begin the 2022 season and fined $5 million for violating the league's personal conduct policy after he was accused by more than two dozen women of sexual assault and sexual misconduct during massage therapy sessions. Two grand juries in Texas declined to pursue criminal charges against him.

In 2023, the Browns lost Watson to a season-ending shoulder injury in Week 10. In 2024, in Week 7, he sustained a torn Achilles tendon in his right leg, forcing him to undergo surgery and then a second surgery after rupturing it again in January 2025. He has gone 9-11 in 20 games as the Browns' starter, including a 34-10 loss to the Jaguars last week in which he threw a touchdown and an interception and was sacked five times. It wasn't even certain that Watson would start in Week 2 until new head coach Todd Monken announced it this week.

Monken was Mayfield's offensive coordinator in Cleveland in 2019. He says he believes he could have done a better job in guiding the Heisman Trophy-winning quarterback. The Browns finished 6-10 that second season.

"I just know the competitor he is, and I've said it all along, I wish I had done a better job in '19," Monken said. "I've said that a lot of times. You've got to own the things you can be better at as a coach. And I'm sure there's certain things that, throughout the course of his life or career, he would look at the same way. Ultimately, I was not here for the rest of it, but I can just tell you that you want your players wired like Baker Mayfield."

Monken applauded Mayfield's play -- which he said has been at an "elite level," along with his competitiveness, and the way he has held himself to a high standard and others to a high standard, describing it as "everything you're looking for in a player ... just in a human being in general."

Mayfield acknowledged some of his own learning lessons from his time with the Browns, with a particular emphasis on his consistency as a leader.

"I think probably the biggest one -- trying to be the same person each and every day for the guys in the locker room, the people you work with, the staff that you're around each day, that some things are out of your control," Mayfield said. "If you're trying to get it fixed and you're not worried about the football aspects of your job, you're probably letting some things slide and fall by the wayside. So I think controlling who I am each and every day, trying to lead the best way possible and control the offense and ultimately win."

Zampese praised Mayfield as a leader and called last week's game a "blip on the radar" and said that there's an even more "heightened awareness" heading into this one, with better ball security, not trying to do too much.

"He's carrying all of us," Zampese said. "He just got rewarded for the job he's done, and we all have great confidence in him doing an even better job as we move forward. And I know he does too."

ESPN's Daniel Oyefusi contributed to this report.

stories.headline: AFL player movement tracker: trade requests, free agency latest, who's on the move?
stories.summary: The offseason is upon us which means AFL trades, free agency, and player movement is about to take off. Here's the latest news, whispers, and confirmed deals.
stories.body:
It's AFL player movement season, with trades and free agency set to dominate the month of October. So who is going where? Keep track with our player movement guide here.

When is the AFL trade and free agency window?
The 2026 AFL trade period commences on Monday, October 5 and closes in the evening of Wednesday, October 14.

The free agency window opens and closes a little ealier; it runs from Friday, October 2 until Friday, October 9.

Thursday, Sept. 17
GWS captain finally makes big call on his future

Toby Greene has opted to leave GWS, telling the AFL club he wishes to play with Geelong next season. Greene, who has been at the Giants since their foundation season in 2012, wants to go back to Victoria for family reasons.

In an extraordinary way to announce the decision, outgoing GWS boss Dave Matthews confirmed Greene's intentions on radio, before the club released a statement.

The 32-year-old has been offered a lucrative three-year deal to join the Cats.

Saturday, Sept. 12
Zak Butters makes huge free agency call
The year's hottest restricted free agent Zak Butters has made a huge call on his future, nominating the Western Bulldogs as his preferred destination.

After a year of speculation, with Geelong thought to be the front-runner for the Power star's signature, Butters made the call on Saturday, first reported by AFL.com.au's Callum Twomey.

The deal is reportedly for nine years.

Thursday, Sept. 10
Hogan set to join Pies
GWS and Collingwood have both confirmed that 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan has chosen the Magpies at his next home.

Set to be a four-club player, Hogan is 31 and coming off a 12-goal season from just nine appearances.

It's a big boost for the Magpies if Hogan can recapture his form; key forward has been an area of concern for a number of years.

Tuesday, Sept. 8
Bailey set to be Lion for life
Brisbane's Zac Bailey has ended months of 'will he, won't he' speculation to sign with the Lions for eight years, taking him through the 2034 season, the the club confirmed on Tuesday.

Bailey, a free agent, had been a big target for the Crows, who had reportedly tabled a more lucrative offer.

"I'm absolutely rapt to be staying at the Brisbane Lions," Bailey said in a statement.

"I love the environment here, the players, coaches and staff who all make it a great place to be and I feel like this Club continues to bring the best out of me.

"This Club means so much to me - I came here as a young player and have grown up here and to know I will be here long-term is something I'm really proud of.

"I would like to thank the club, my partner Em, my family and my management for being so supportive throughout this process.

"I love what we as a club have achieved during my time here and I am super excited about what we can continue to achieve together."

Rowan Marshall requests trade
St Kilda ruck Rowan Marshall looks set to be on the move, with the Saints confirming the big man had requested a trade for the second straight season.

While Marshall hasn't requested a specific club, it's likely to be Geelong after he failed to secure a trade to the Cats last year. He played 21 games for the Saints this seaosn, juggling ruck duties with Tom De Koning, who came in from Carlton last offseason.

"Rowan is a highly valued member of the St Kilda Football Club and remains contracted until the end of 2027," the Saints said in a statement.

"Marshall has not nominated a preferred destination at this stage, with the club making clear that any trade will need to be in the best interests of the St Kilda Football Club."

Zane Duursma wants to go to Melbourne
The No. 4 pick in the 2023 AFL draft Zane Duursma has requested a trade out of North Melbourne, with Melbourne in his sights.

The news comes a week after coach Alastair Clarkson was sacked by the club. North won nine games in 2026, their best return since 2019.

Ed Allan re-signs with the Pies
After speculation about his future at the Magpies, mdifielder Ed Allan has put pen to paper, signing a four year extension to remain at Collingwood.

2026 was a breakout season for Allan, who played 19 games and averaged a career-high 16.5 disposals per game.

Monday, Sept. 7
Pair of in-demand Dogs re-sign
According to afl.com.au, both Arty Jones and Buku Khamis will remain at the Kennel this offseason.

Jones will sign a three-year deal, while Khamis has a five-year contract in front of him.

Essendon and Brisbane had interest in livewire forward Jones, who had a standout performance against Collingwood in the wildcard final win, while the Blues were heavily linked to Khamis for a second straight offseason.

Cooper Hodge nomintes Hawthorn
A big boost for the Hawks, with club champion Luke Hodge's son Cooper choosing to join the Melbourne-based team as a father-son at this year's draft.

He had the option of going to Brisbane as a Lions academy member.

stories.headline: Boehly, Walter sell Chelsea stakes as Clearlake takes full control
stories.summary: Clearlake Capital has taken full control of Chelsea after acquiring the ownership stakes of Mark Walter and Todd Boehly, the Premier League club announced Wednesday.
stories.body:
Todd Boehly and fellow co-owner Mark Walter have sold their stakes in Chelsea in a deal that gives Clearlake Capital full control of the English Premier League club.

Private equity firm Clearlake, led by Behdad Eghbali and Jose E. Feliciano, previously owned a 61.5% stake in Chelsea, while U.S. businessmen Walter and Boehly each owned 12.83%. The club said in Wednesday's announcement that Swiss philanthropist Hansjörg Wyss, who also owned a 12.83% stake, will remain a partner in the ownership group.

The consortium bought Chelsea for £2.5 billion ($3.3 billion) in 2022 with a further £1.75 billion ($2.3 billion) committed to investment in the club after former owner Roman Abramovich was sanctioned by alleged ties to Russia president Vladimir Putin following the country's invasion of Ukraine.

The Financial Times reported that Walter and Boehly will receive £950 million ($1.3 billion) for their combined stake in a deal that values the club at £5 billion ($6.7 billion) including debt.

Boehly also held the position of club chairman, a role which he will now relinquish.

Chelsea said chairman Boehly had shown "unwavering commitment" to the ownership group's belief that the supporters are at the heart of the club.

"It has been an honour to serve as Chairman of Chelsea Football Club," Boehly said in a Chelsea statement. "I would like to thank the many who helped secure a bright future for the Club, including the English Premier League, the coaches and players, the talented leadership and staff at Chelsea, and the legions of dedicated fans.

"I have valued my partnership with Clearlake and the wider ownership group, and the collective decisions and investment we have made to support the immediate and long-term success of the Club. I am confident that Chelsea is well positioned for continued success under Clearlake's leadership."

ESPN reported last month that the relationship between Clearlake and other investors, specifically Boehly, deteriorated over recent years with each looking to buy the other out in 2024.

Walter last month completed the sudden sale of the Los Angeles Lakers to venture capitalist Joshua Kushner and former Disney CEO Bob Iger at a $12.5 billion valuation.

Walter, who only acquired the Lakers 14 months earlier, is under federal investigation relating to insurance companies he owns. He remains owner of the Los Angeles Dodgers.

Chelsea, who appointed Xabi Alonso as manager in the summer and are currently sixth in the Premier League, said there will be no changes to day-to-day operations, leadership or strategy at the club.

Information from ESPN's James Olley and PA contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Max Verstappen wins Max vs 100 in style after overtaking 100 go-karters in 35 minutes
stories.summary: Max Verstappen stormed through a field of 100 karters to win Max vs 100 in remarkable fashion as the four-time Formula 1 world champion made light work of the unique challenge at Silverstone.
stories.body:
Max Verstappen stormed through a field of 100 karters to win Max vs 100 in remarkable fashion as the four-time Formula 1 world champion made light work of the unique challenge at Silverstone.

Verstappen was given 30 laps, or 75 minutes, to overtake 100 drivers from the back of the grid in a go-kart race but only needed 13 laps, and 35 minutes, to add the latest win to his motorsport collection.

- As it happened: Relive Max vs 100 as Verstappen took on 10 karters

- HIGHLIGHTS: Watch the best bits from Max vs 100 on ESPN's YouTube

On a modified karting circuit at the home of F1 in the UK, Verstappen -- after starting 101st -- overtook 63 drivers on the very first lap, including ESPN's Nate Saunders, who barely lasted 10 seconds. Drivers clashed, spun around and ultimately watched Verstappen sail past as the predicted carnage ensued on Lap 1, resulting in waved yellow flags.

After that, Verstappen continued to carve his way through the field at an alarming rate, while also speaking to the competitors -- made up of athletes, content creators, journalists and other celebrities -- along the way.

"I'm coming for you," he said to a contestant at one stage. Later, he told commentators: "They need to focus because I'm definitely catching them."

It took Verstappen 15 minutes to get up to P7, and while at that stage he was still 14 seconds behind the runaway top three -- journalist Jacky Martens, YouTuber Zac Alsop and Red Bull's own Lewis Osler -- he quickly gained at a rate of around three seconds-a-lap.

The top three were given an extra 'fast lap' -- a shortcut of the circuit -- but that wasn't enough to catch Verstappen and he completed the challenge in style on Lap 13.

"My first lap was quite incredible," Verstappen said afterwards. "There was a lot happening and actually a few cars got stuck and I always managed to be on the other side, so didn't get stuck.

"And that made me get like 60 people in the first lap. So that just helps a lot, getting through to the front."

Asked where the win ranks in his victories, he said: "I think this is the best one yet!"

Saunders, meanwhile, was less positive post-race comments -- but nonetheless was impressed by the Dutchman.

"That was all a bit of a blur," he said. "Shortly after the start I looked to my right and there was Max -- and then he was gone. The way he was able to zigzag through the crowd was crazy."

The event was streamed live globally on ESPN on Disney+, while Verstappen will next be in action at F1's Azerbaijan Grand Prix. The Red Bull star is sixth in the drivers' championship.

stories.headline: Borussia Dortmund teenager Konstantinos Karetsas returns to training after Champions League health scare
stories.summary: Borussia Dortmund says 18-year-old midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas is back in training just over a week after he slumped to the ground in an alarming medical incident on his Champions League debut.
stories.body:
Borussia Dortmund have said 18-year-old midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas is back in training just over a week after he slumped to the ground in an alarming medical incident on his Champions League debut.

Karetsas passed the ball to a teammate then signaled his distress to the referee before sitting on the grass during Dortmund's 3-2 win over Villarreal on Sept. 8.

He was in tears as he was stretchered off with suspected circulatory problems and was then taken to a hospital, where he stayed for much of last week.

"Konstantinos Karetsas is back in team training as of Wednesday after doing individual sessions at the start of the week," Dortmund said. "It was his first joint session with his teammates after he was taken off with circulatory problems in the game against Villarreal."

Dortmund hasn't specified the nature of any diagnosis for Karetsas, who was signed from Genk for a reported fee of $34.6 million last month, and didn't indicate whether he would be able to play Saturday against Stuttgart in the Bundesliga.

Karetsas plays internationally for Greece but was born in Belgium, where local media have reported that dehydration was suspected as a factor.

"I'm doing really well," he said in a video recorded during a visit to his old club Genk and published Monday on X. "We tested everything and everything is fine. I just need to adjust a bit to the intensity but that will come with time."

"I went out with him but in that moment, he wasn't able to speak," Book said.

- Borussia Dortmund teenager Karetsas hospitalised after slumping to turf in Champions League

Karetsas was able to cheer on his teammates from the stands in Saturday's 3-0 win over Paderborn.

Managing director Lars Ricken said there had been "no warning signs" of any circulatory problems prior to the incident.

stories.headline: Alexa Grasso shows off flyweight's elite status in women's P4P top 10
stories.summary: Former UFC champion puts elite status of women's flyweight division on display in ESPN's P4P top 10.
stories.body:
It's uncommon for two fighters ranked in the pound-for-pound top 10 to meet in a bout with no championship at stake. But that was the case at Saturday's fourth annual Noche UFC, where Alexa Grasso faced Manon Fiorot.

Grasso is a former women's flyweight champion and Fiorot competed for the belt last year, so their status as MMA elites was well established before they fought. And when Grasso won by unanimous decision, she further solidified her standing in the ESPN women's pound-for-pound rankings.

The top five of the rankings remains intact, and Grasso moves up from 10th to replace Fiorot at No. 6. Fiorot slips two positions to No. 8 in a pound-for-pound hierarchy in which seven of the 10 ranked women compete at flyweight (including Zhang Weili, the former UFC strawweight champion who last fought in an unsuccessful challenge of Valentina Shevchenko in November).

With Shevchenko injured and having vacated her title, there will be much scrambling for the top spot, which will be at stake when No. 5 Natalia Silva fights unranked Wang Cong on Oct. 3.

For the ESPN divisional MMA rankings, click here.

Note: Results are current; rankings are as of Sept. 16. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

Women's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Valentina Shevchenko

UFC flyweight

Record: 26-4-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Zhang Weili, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

Shevchenko's dominance came under question in 2022 and 2023, when she went 1-1-1 in a trilogy with Alexa Grasso. Boy, does that feel like a long time ago now. Shevchenko more than reasserted herself as the best flyweight in the world, and then she established herself as the No. 1 woman in the world, period. It wasn't surprising that she beat Zhang, but it was surprising how easy she made it look. Shevchenko is out injured, however, so she has vacated her UFC title, which will be up for grabs when Natalia Silva meets Wang Cong on Oct. 3.

2. Zhang Weili

UFC flyweight / strawweight

Record: 26-4

Last: L (UD) vs. Valentina Shevchenko, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

It's hard to move up in weight, especially at the highest level. That sounds like it should be obvious, but Zhang had been dominant at 115 pounds for so long, some of us might have taken for granted how big of a challenge moving to 125 would be. UFC 322 was a bad night for Zhang, but she doesn't have many. And if she decides to stay at flyweight, it certainly seems reasonable to believe she'll fare better in the future.

3. Cris Cyborg

PFL featherweight champion

Record: 30-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Ketlen Vieira, Aug. 22

Next: TBA

It had been a while since Cyborg had fought an elite opponent in MMA until she met Larissa Pacheco in 2024. That was a legitimate matchup -- and many within the industry were predicting Cyborg's downfall. Instead, she took out the PFL's two-weight champion, upending all of Pacheco's momentum. One of the original pioneers of women's MMA is once again a champion after getting her second career submission at PFL Lyon in December. The PFL promoted her fight with Vieira as a retirement bout, but after her win Cyborg did not sound like someone who is done fighting.

4. Mackenzie Dern

UFC strawweight champion

Record: 17-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Gillian Robertson, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Dern's rise to the 115-pound throne was truly a changing of the guard. She is the division's first first-time champion since 2019, because the previous three champs -- Zhang Weili, Carla Esparza and Rose Namajunas -- all were in their second reigns. Dern, nearly a decade into her MMA career after multiple jiu-jitsu world championships, has won four fights in a row, including a dominant performance against a fellow grappling-heavy fighter, Robertson, in her first title defense.

5. Natalia Silva

UFC flyweight

Record: 20-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Rose Namajunas, Jan. 24

Next: Oct. 3 vs. Wang Cong

Silva is looking every bit the part of a future UFC champion following a dominant display against Alexa Grasso at UFC 315 and a victory over Namajunas at UFC 324. Silva's stick-and-move style has frustrated even the highest level of opponent, and she's got youth on her side as she won't turn 30 until 2027. With an injured Valentina Shevchenko having vacated the title, Silva will fight Wang for the belt at UFC 332.

6. Alexa Grasso

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 10

Record: 18-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Manon Fiorot, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Grasso went nearly three years without winning a fight, but her 2023 win right before the skid was a huge one, a submission of Valentina Shevchenko for the UFC title. What followed were two more fights with Shevchenko -- a draw, then a loss -- and then a loss to Natalia Silva. But she reasserted herself with a finish of Maycee Barber in March, then got the best of Fiorot, a fellow title contender, at Noche UFC to put herself in position for another title shot.

7. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL flyweight

Record: 16-0

Last: W (UD) vs. Denise Kielholtz, July 31

Next: TBA

Not only did Ditcheva win the PFL's flyweight season in 2024, but she did so in spectacular fashion -- a TKO finish over Taila Santos, who once challenged for a UFC title. Ditcheva fought only once in 2025, dominating Sumiko Inaba in the co-main event of the first PFL Champions Series card in Cape Town, South Africa. She then spent over a year on the sideline, healing injuries to both hands, before returning at PFL New York with a dominant win over Kielholtz.

8. Manon Fiorot

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 6

Record: 13-3

Last: L (UD) vs. Alexa Grasso, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Fiorot had handled everyone the UFC put in front of her -- except the champion, Valentina Shevchenko, who defeated the Frenchwoman at UFC 315 in May 2025. But then, with another title shot within her grasp, Fiorot ran into Grasso, a former champion, at Noche UFC and lost a competitive fight.

9. Erin Blanchfield

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 8

Record: 14-2

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Tracy Cortez, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: Oct. 17 vs. Jasmine Jasudavicius

Her rise toward the top of the division was derailed by a March 2024 loss to Manon Fiorot, but Blanchfield bounced back with two straight wins, including one over two-time former strawweight champion Rose Namajunas in November 2024. If she wins her October bout with Jasudavicius, a fellow top-10 flyweight contender, Blanchfield would inch ever closer to a title shot.

10. Tatiana Suarez

UFC strawweight

Previous ranking: 9

Record: 12-1

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Loopy Godínez, April 11

Next: TBA

If Suarez is still feeling the effects of last year's humbling defeat to Zhang Weili in a title challenge, she certainly didn't show it at UFC 327, overcoming early adversity to thrash Godinez, a fellow top-10 strawweight. Suarez is going to be a tough out for anyone at 115 pounds.

Men's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Islam Makhachev

UFC welterweight champion

Record: 29-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Ian Machado Garry, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Makhachev vacated the UFC lightweight championship to go for a second title at welterweight. By winning that belt last November with a thrashing of Jack Della Maddalena, Makhachev staked his place among MMA's greatest -- not just in today's sport but of all time. His win over Machado Garry at UFC 330 was his 17th straight, breaking the UFC record for consecutive wins. Makhachev is piling up unprecedented achievements.

2. Petr Yan

UFC bantamweight champion

Record: 20-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Merab Dvalishvili, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Dvalishvili

What a return to the top it's been for Yan. He began his career with 15 consecutive wins before going on a 1-4 run from 2021 to 2023. That almost doesn't feel real now, after watching him reclaim his throne against Dvalishvili, who once handed him the worst loss of his career. Yan took a major detour, but this was the destination we felt he was capable of before the skid. He once again looks like one of the best fighters on the planet. He can prove it by beating Dvalishvili again.

3. Merab Dvalishvili

UFC bantamweight

Record: 21-5

Last: L (UD) vs. Petr Yan, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Yan

Dvalishvili was on one of the most impressive runs through the UFC's bantamweight division ever. Not only did he defeat Sean O'Malley for the second time in nine months at UFC 316, but he showcased a new part of his game, finishing O'Malley with a guillotine. Starting in August 2022, Dvalishvili beat José Aldo, Yan, Henry Cejudo, O'Malley (twice), Umar Nurmagomedov and Cory Sandhagen. But at UFC 323, in an attempt to become the first champion in UFC history to successfully defend a title four times in a calendar year, Dvalishvili lost a rematch with Yan. They will fight for a third time at UFC 333.

4. Tom Aspinall

UFC heavyweight

Record: 15-3, 1 NC

Last: NC1 vs. Ciryl Gane, Oct. 25, 2025

Next: TBA

You can make a case that Aspinall is the most dynamic, skillful, talented heavyweight the sport has seen. He is dominating opponents in a way that is unmatched. No one can last a round with him. He had hoped to prove his supremacy against Jon Jones, but Jones opted to retire, elevating Aspinall from interim champion. His first defense of the undisputed belt ended anticlimactically, as an eye poke resulted in his UFC 321 fight with Gane being declared a no-contest. Still recovering from the eye injury, Aspinall vacated his title on Sept. 14.

5. Ilia Topuria

UFC lightweight

Record: 17-1

Last: L (TKO4) vs. Justin Gaethje, June 14

Next: TBA

Topuria was an undefeated two-division champion when he ran into Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250 and was brutalized in a stoppage loss. How will that affect the immediate future of Topuria? His knockout wins over two of the greatest featherweights, Alexander Volkanovski and Max Holloway, gave him an intimidating aura. Can the former champion get that back?

6. Justin Gaethje

UFC lightweight champion

Record: 28-5

Last: W (TKO4) vs. Ilia Topuria, June 14

Next: TBA

Gaethje has spent his 15-year career thrilling MMA fans, but before the title bout on the White House lawn, all he had to show for it -- aside from 15 bonus checks in 15 UFC appearances -- were two missed opportunities to be an undisputed champion. His fourth-round TKO of Topuria got Gaethje over the hump. It was a resilient performance in a back-and-forth battle that is a prime candidate for fight of the year. More important for Gaethje: At age 37, he is finally sitting at the top of the mountain.

7. Alexander Volkanovski

UFC featherweight champion

Record: 28-4

Last: W (UD) vs. Diego Lopes, Jan. 31

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Movsar Evloev

It felt as if the sport had started to write Volkanovski's eulogy following his knockout loss to Ilia Topuria in February 2024. Volkanovski noticed and made a point of proving to everyone he still has plenty left by recapturing the featherweight belt at UFC 314, the first of two consecutive wins over Lopes. His age (37) will likely continue to be a prefight topic, which is fine because Volkanovski enjoys proving people wrong. Can he hand Evloev his first loss at UFC 333?

8. Alexandre Pantoja

UFC flyweight

Record: 30-6

Last: L (TKO1) vs. Joshua Van, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Sept. 19 vs. Joshua Van

Pantoja became the UFC's unquestioned flyweight king by racking up four title defenses, including two in pay-per-view main events in 2024. He built his winning streak to eight in his UFC 317 win over Kai Kara-France, whom he had already defeated before, like other challengers. But he lost his belt in a gruesome way, injuring his elbow in the opening seconds of a UFC 323 fight with Van. Pantoja gets his rematch with Van at UFC 331.

9. Ciryl Gane

UFC heavyweight interim champion

Record: 14-2, 1 NC

Last: W (TKO2) vs. Alex Pereira, June 14

Next: TBA

Gane is unique in that he is the first -- and could very well go down as the only -- heavyweight to face the division's four biggest names in Francis Ngannou, Jon Jones, Tom Aspinall and Pereira. None of those four have fought each other, yet all four have have fought the Frenchman. Gane was 0-2 with a no-contest against that group before he knocked out Pereira in the second round of their interim title fight. Gane was heralded as the future of the generation when he broke onto the scene, but endured growing pains in losses to Ngannou and Jones. He looks formidable now, and no one will be counting him out if he faces Aspinall in a title unification bout.

10. Alex Pereira

UFC heavyweight / light heavyweight

Record: 13-4

Last: L (TKO2) vs. Ciryl Gane, June 14

Next: TBA

He was on the verge of making history when the opportunity fell apart. Pereira was a UFC champion at middleweight, then light heavyweight, but his unprecedented pursuit of a belt in a third weight class did not go well for the Brazilian, who lost an interim heavyweight title fight to Gane on the White House card. At 39 years old, Pereira does not have much time left to recapture the magic.

Other fighters receiving votes: Joshua Van and Arman Tsarukyan.

stories.headline: NRL Midweek Mail semifinals: Mulitalo relishing rematch, Katoa on possible Sharks curtain call
stories.summary: Ronaldo Mulitalo is determined to honour his departing Sharks teammates, Sione Katoa has opened up about his future at the Cowboys and his finals days at the Sharks, while Nathan Cleary is fighting the clock to be fit for Penrith's prelim.
stories.body:
The NRL rarely stands still.

Between training sessions, media appearances, and behind-the-scenes conversations, new storylines often begin to emerge before the weekend arrives.

Throughout the week, ESPN will be gathering notes, insights, and updates from around the competition heading into the NRL's semifinal week.

Mulitalo relishing 'Marky Mark' rematch

Ronaldo Mulitalo is embracing another blockbuster battle with Roosters star Mark Nawaqanitawase, describing the departing winger as a "generational talent".

Mulitalo said Nawaqanitawase "brings the best out of me" and revealed their on-field rivalry is largely one-sided when it comes to the verbal exchanges.

"He's a gentleman out there... he doesn't really say anything. I think it's more myself," Mulitalo joked. "He knows I'm just going to keep talking, so he just ignores me anyway."

Mulitalo determined to honour departing Sharks

Ronaldo Mulitalo says Cronulla's finals run carries added significance with several longtime teammates set to leave the club at season's end.

Mulitalo said he has played alongside some of the departing Sharks since he was 16 and wants to "honour those boys" with his performance against the Roosters.

"I don't want to let them down and disappoint them, winning the game is the most important part of the week for me."

Katoa reveals Cowboys appeal

Sione Katoa has revealed North Queensland's attacking style was a major attraction behind his move to the Cowboys in 2027.

After helping eliminate his future club from the finals, Katoa told ESPN he "loves the style of footy" they play, describing it as "free footy" and similar to Cronulla's attack.

Katoa emotional over Sharks farewell
He also admitted the reality that every game could be his last for Cronulla is beginning to sink in.

"Tonight might have been the last week, maybe the last game," he told ESPN after scoring a double against North Queensland.

"I'm very happy right now that I get another week with my brothers and play again."

Cleary racing clock for preliminary final

Nathan Cleary is in doubt for Penrith's preliminary final after scans revealed an stress-related bone issue in his foot.

The Panthers will assess and monitor their star halfback over the next fortnight, with their week off providing valuable recovery time.

Cleary has, however, been cleared of any suspension concern after receiving only a Grade 1 Dangerous Contact charge for his incident with Hugo Savala.

stories.headline: Cristian 'Kily' González arrives to take charge of Messi, Miami
stories.summary: New Inter Miami head coach Cristian "Kily" González said he feels blessed at being given the opportunity to lead the club and coach Lionel Messi, after formerly taking up the role on Tuesday.
stories.body:
FORT LAUDERDALE, Fla. -- New Inter Miami head coach Cristian "Kily" González said he feels blessed at being given the opportunity to lead the club and coach Lionel Messi, after formerly taking up the role on Tuesday.

González has now received the authorization to begin the job after being announced last month as the permanent replacement for interim coach Guillermo Hoyos on a contract through June 2028.

- Source: Colombia targeting U.S. U20 dual national Shaw

- Messi tracker: All goals, assists, key moments for Miami, Argentina in 2026

- Messi scores, but Nashville strikes late to deny Miami win

The job sees him reunite with Messi after the two shared the field for Argentina in two World Cup qualifiers in 2005.

"There are things in football that simply cannot be described in words; they are unique feelings. I feel privileged and blessed to have this opportunity and to share the fantastic relationship I have with Leo," González said in a news conference.

"I adore him, he knows it, and that makes this moment even more special. Being with him and sharing experiences with the incredible players on this squad. Honestly, as a coach, I feel completely fulfilled.

"Of course, this is all wonderful, but now we have to get to work. God willing, we'll start off strong tomorrow and win the championship."

González led his first training session with Inter Miami on Tuesday after landing in Miami from Argentina earlier in the morning. He will be on the sidelines for the team's Campeones Cup match against Liga MX champions Cruz Azul on Wednesday night at Nu Stadium.

Inter Miami reached an agreement with González on Aug. 27, but the coach could not take over for Hoyos until receiving his work permit.

"What were these past few days like? To be honest, they were filled with a lot of anticipation. It had been nearly two and a half weeks and I couldn't be here, but this unique opportunity, something I hadn't even dared to dream of, became a reality," González said.

"We spoke with the club, and they offered me the chance to join the team; I said yes immediately. Being with the players, seeing their willingness to welcome my coaching staff, and watching them train the way they did today honestly, it made me very happy and gave me a huge boost of energy for tomorrow's match."

Miami's opponent in the Campeones Cup was delayed in arriving in Miami for the game and instead of landing in the U.S. on Monday, were unable to fly in until Tuesday.

"Well, more than an odyssey, sometimes accidents like this happen, and you just have to turn the page," said Cruz Azul manager Joel Huiqui. "The team is doing well. We rested very well yesterday, we stayed at a hotel in Mexico, and we're just arriving now. We're calm, obviously aware that tomorrow will be a huge match for us, and we're all focused.

"It goes without saying that [Messis] is a great player, but what matters most to me is that the team realizes what is at stake: not just another trophy, but our consolidation as an institution. Beyond the chance to face a great player, the opportunity to win the title against a team like Inter Miami is about solidifying the work we've been doing and, above all, bringing joy to the fans."

Inter Miami currently sits in second place on the Eastern Conference table with 45 points in 25 games. The team has recorded just one victory in its last nine games.

Inter Miami forward Luis Suárez said he wants to use the game against Cruz Azul to start strong under new leadership.

"When it comes to playing a match like this, it's a final. There is no time to dwell on the past, the only thing that matters is looking ahead to tomorrow," Suárez said. "We've come through a challenging run of games, but now we face the best possible scenario: playing a final and moving forward with a new coach who brings great positive energy, a strong desire to grow and plenty of enthusiasm.

"That attitude is contagious, and we are ready to support him and his coaching staff."

Inter Miami hosts Cruz Azul before returning to Major League Soccer regular season action on Sunday against San Diego.

stories.headline: Washington Commanders unveil first renderings inside new stadium
stories.summary: In the latest renderings of the new stadium, the Commanders point to RFK with the intent of re-creating a "loud, intense and intimate atmosphere."
stories.body:
ASHBURN, Va. -- The Washington Commanders continue to focus on their past while moving forward with their new stadium.

They want to re-create the home-field advantage they enjoyed at RFK Stadium from 1961 to 1996 before they moved to their current home, Northwest Stadium in Landover, Maryland.

In the latest renderings of the new stadium, designed by global design firm HKS and scheduled to open in 2030 at the site where RFK once stood, the Commanders point to RFK with the intent of re-creating a "loud, intense and intimate atmosphere," according to a news release on Wednesday.

Of course, part of that home-field advantage was a result of the team's success. While playing at RFK, Washington made five trips to the Super Bowl with three victories. (It won Super Bowls during the 1982, 1987 and 1991 campaigns.) From 1971 to 1992, the organization posted 18 winning seasons.

While playing in Landover, Washington has posted eight winning seasons and been to the NFC Championship Game once.

As shown previously, the latest renderings include a cantilevered, translucent roof that is somewhat similar to the one at U.S. Bank Stadium, where the Minnesota Vikings play. That stadium was also designed by HKS. And as with that stadium, there will be a glass facade, in this case offering a view of the U.S. Capitol.

But the focus inside has been on creating a louder environment. The seating bowl on both sides rises straight up; the goal is to have minimal overhangs that can prevent sound from being absorbed. Team officials have mentioned in the past how they liked this feature at the Kansas City Chiefs' Arrowhead Stadium.

The stadium will also have a "Wall of Fans" -- similar to what the NBA's LA Clippers have done at Intuit Dome. It's a section behind one end zone that the organization said will include "affordable fan-friendly seating."

The stadium will be one continuous loop and will seat about 65,000 fans. It cost nearly $4 billion, with the Commanders contributing $2.7 billion and $1.1 billion coming from taxpayers.

After 29 years of playing in a stadium that lacked a home-field advantage, it's clear what the Commanders and HKS wanted in their future home. At RFK, one section included stands that would bounce when the crowd in that area got excited. The new stadium will have a section that will bounce as well.

Washington team president Mark Clouse said: "Every aspect of the design is intended to amplify the energy and intensity of the crowd."

stories.headline: Man United will be 'careful' with Gabriel future, Carrick says
stories.summary: Michael Carrick confirmed he is involved in conversations about JJ Gabriel's future after the 15-year-old's request to leave Manchester United made major ripples and that the team is being "careful" with the situation.
stories.body:
Michael Carrick confirmed he is involved in conversations about JJ Gabriel's future after the 15-year-old's request to leave Manchester United made major ripples and that the team is being "careful" with the situation.

Fresh from scoring a hat trick for the Under-19s on his UEFA Youth League debut last Thursday, the highly-rated forward was set to be included in the senior squad for the first time in a competitive match on Wednesday.

But Gabriel was not involved in United's 3-2 Carabao Cup collapse to Brighton after it emerged on the eve of the tie that the teenager's camp had made a request for him to leave the Old Trafford club.

Asked about the situation surrounding the 15-year-old after the third-round loss, boss Carrick said: "I just think we've got to be really careful of the whole situation.

"He's a young boy, he's 15 and the biggest [thing] for me definitely and as a club point of view is looking after our younger players. Their welfare, their wellbeing, their exposure.

"And I think all of us we've got to be really conscious of that, really, in this situation.

"As a club, for sure, we're all involved in those conversations. I just think we've got to be very careful of that."

Sources told ESPN that Barcelona and Real Madrid are among the clubs monitoring Gabriel's stand-off with Manchester United, sources have told ESPN, with his stance opening the door to a departure next summer.

Gabriel is eligible to sign scholarship forms after his 16th birthday, which is on Oct. 6.

Spanish giants Barcelona and Real Madrid have both been alerted to the situation, with Gabriel able to move to a European side because he has an Irish passport.

Information from ESPN writer Rob Dawson and PA was used in this report.

stories.headline: Sources: Jessica Campbell, Bryan McCabe latest to join Devils
stories.summary: The Devils are hiring former Kraken assistant coach Jessica Campbell as manager of player development and longtime Panthers executive Bryan McCabe as vice president of prospect personnel, sources told ESPN.
stories.body:
The New Jersey Devils are hiring former Seattle Kraken assistant coach Jessica Campbell as manager of player development and longtime Florida Panthers executive Bryan McCabe as vice president of prospect personnel, sources told ESPN.

Campbell, 34, became the first woman to serve as a full-time coach behind an NHL bench. She was promoted to Seattle in 2024 after helping the AHL's Coachella Valley Firebirds reach back-to-back Calder Cup Finals.

After her playing career, Campbell became a power skating and skills coach, working privately with NHL players before coaching professionally in Sweden and Germany.

McCabe, 51, will also serve as an assistant general manager for the Devils' AHL affiliate in Utica. He spent 14 years in the Panthers' front office, specializing in player development and personnel.

A longtime NHL defenseman, McCabe played 1,135 games and served as Panthers captain before moving into management. He was part of Florida's back-to-back Stanley Cup championships before leaving this summer when his contract expired.

McCabe is the third former Panthers executive to join Sunny Mehta in New Jersey. Mehta spent six seasons in Florida's front office before being named Devils GM in April. He has also hired former Panthers executive Braden Birch as assistant GM and Leo Luongo as director of goaltending.

stories.headline: UFC's Islam Makhachev questions validity of Jon Jones' wins streak
stories.summary: UFC champ Islam Makhachev believes Jon Jones' failed drug tests and issues outside the Octagon invalidate Jones' place among the UFC's all-time streaks for consecutive wins.
stories.body:
Jon Jones and Islam Makhachev, two of the greatest fighters in UFC history, are taking shots at each other this week.

Makhachev (29-1) broke the UFC's official win streak record in August, when he defended his welterweight championship against Ian Machado Garry for his 17th consecutive win. Former middleweight champion Anderson Silva held the previous record of 16. Jones, a former light heavyweight and heavyweight champion, would argue he won 20 bouts in a row from 2010 to 2024, but his streak was interrupted by a no-contest against Daniel Cormier in 2017.

In a recent interview with a Russian news outlet, Makhachev said Jones' no-contest, which was the result of a failed drug test by the United States Anti-Doping Agency, invalidates his win streak.

"I'm not denying that Jon Jones is one of the greatest athletes in history, but he was caught doping twice," Makhachev told Ushatayka. "I think that's why his streak isn't considered valid. Because he went into a fight while on PEDs and won, that's where a new count should have started."

Jonse (28-1) was fined and suspended 15 months for testing positive for extremely trace amounts of steroid metabolites. He initially defeated Cormier in their fight in 2017, before it was later changed to a no-contest.

An independent arbitrator later stated he believed Jones unknowingly ingested the substance and that it was not performance enhancing. Jones has long pointed to that independent finding as validation of his innocence, and did so again Monday in a post directed at Makhachev.

"If you believe USADA for finding a picogram in my system, then you must believe USADA when they say it 'It was not found to be PERFORMANCE ENHANCING or INTENTIONAL,'" Jones wrote on X. "You can't have it both ways. Last I checked, my hand got raised every time I was in the Octagon since any of you can remember. Your own coach said I was 'a gift from God.' Let's not forget you've been KO'd, flatlined, went night night."

Makhachev, whose only loss came by knockout to Adriano Martins in his second UFC fight in 2015, responded to Jones the following day, and hinted at Jones's troubled legal history, both in and out of competition.

"Jon, I'm not trying to diminish your achievements in any way," Makhachev wrote on X. "But your whole life seems to be tied to breaking the rules one way or another, and somehow, you're never the one to be blamed."

stories.headline: Warriors sell out Eden Park in 48 hours amid NRL's crowd woes
stories.summary: Hooker Sam Healey plans to draw inspiration from his rugby league idol to help him handle the pulsating atmosphere of a sold-out Eden Park.
stories.body:
Hooker Sam Healey plans to draw inspiration from his NRL idol to help him handle the pulsating atmosphere of a sold-out Eden Park.

The NRL announced that general-public tickets for Sunday's do-or-die semi-final between the Warriors and Newcastle in Auckland had sold out in less than 48 hours.

It comes after New Zealand were forced to relocate from their traditional home ground for the clash because Eden Park hosts about 25,000 more spectators than Go Media Stadium.

The 50,000-seat venue being full comes after the league was criticised over poor crowd numbers in the first week of finals, although the Warriors had a mostly sold-out attendance for their 26-16 loss to the Dolphins.

Regardless, it's the club's first clash at Eden Park since 2014, and will be a mammoth moment for New Zealand rugby league as the Warriors look to keep alive their hopes of a first premiership.

Healey is yet to play at the venue, but will be wanting to produce similar heroics to his idol Kevin Locke, who made a courageous try-saving tackle on Sydney Roosters centre Michael Jennings at the Fortress in 2013.

"I have played league since I was five or six or something like that, so I always loved the game," Healey said.

"I actually saw him (Locke) in the sheds the other day, and I said to my mum, 'Do you remember when he was my favourite player'. She just started laughing.

"He used to be my lock-screen on my phone ... I just said g'day."

Warriors back-rower Jacob Laban has only played once at the country's biggest sporting stadium.

"It was Kiwi A's versus Tonga A's, I think it was two, three years ago," he said.

"(After) New Zealand played Samoa (in the Pacific Championships) ... it was a pretty cool, good atmosphere.

"Obviously it (the crowd) is a little bit further (away) than Mt Smart, but it's not too bad. When you score a try, you can walk up to the fans over there, so it's still pretty close."

Laban won't be intimidated by the history of Eden Park, although the club has won only one of its six games at the venue.

The blond second-rower is intent on not just helping the Warriors set up a preliminary final against Penrith, but also on making his childhood self proud.

"I knew I wanted to play for the Warriors when I first heard about rugby league," Laban said.

"They came to Wellington. I don't know what year it was, but I still have this photo of me where I had half a Warriors face painted on and a Warriors T-shirt.

"I knew I wanted to play for the Warriors since I was young."
